subtopic: Properties of inequalities of sides and angles of a triangle
stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), If \(PQ > PR\) and bisectors of \(\angle Q\) and \(\angle R\) intersect at S. Show that \(SQ > SR\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.58 — \(\triangle PQR\) with P at the apex, Q lower-left, R lower-right. The bisectors of \(\angle Q\) and \(\angle R\) are drawn dashed and meet at S inside the triangle; two small circles mark the two halves of \(\angle Q\) and two crosses mark the two halves of \(\angle R\).
_note: The printed stem does not cite the figure by number, but Fig. 3.58 is printed beside this question. The stem is self-contained (S is defined in words), so the figure is illustrative.

stem: In figure 3.59, point D and E are on side BC of \(\triangle ABC\), such that \(BD = CE\) and \(AD = AE\). Show that \(\triangle ABD \cong \triangle ACE\). (In the figure the points lie in the order B - D - E - C.)
diagramNote: Fig. 3.59 — \(\triangle ABC\) with A at the apex and B, C at the base. D and E lie on BC in the order B - D - E - C. Single tick marks on BD and EC show \(BD = CE\); seg AD and seg AE are drawn dashed with double tick marks showing \(AD = AE\).

subtopic: Properties of inequalities of sides and angles of a triangle
stem: In figure 3.60, point S is any point on side QR of \(\triangle PQR\). Prove that : \(PQ + QR + RP > 2PS\)
diagramNote: Fig. 3.60 — \(\triangle PQR\) with P at the top, Q lower-left and R lower-right. S is a point on side QR (Q - S - R) and seg PS is drawn. No other marks.

subtopic: Properties of inequalities of sides and angles of a triangle
stem: In figure 3.61, bisector of \(\angle BAC\) intersects side BC at point D. Prove that \(AB > BD\)
diagramNote: Fig. 3.61 — \(\triangle ABC\) with A at the top-left, B lower-left and C far right. D lies on side BC (B - D - C) and seg AD is drawn; two small circles at A, one on each side of AD, mark \(\angle BAD = \angle DAC\).

stem: In figure 3.62, seg PT is the bisector of \(\angle QPR\). A line parallel to seg PT and passing through R intersects ray QP at point S. Prove that \(PS = PR\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.62 — \(\triangle PQR\) with Q lower-left, R lower-right and P above. Ray QP is extended beyond P to S (order Q - P - S). Seg PT is drawn dashed to T on QR, with two crosses at P marking \(\angle QPT = \angle TPR\); seg RS is drawn dashed and is parallel to seg PT.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem: In figure 3.63, seg AD \(\perp\) seg BC. seg AE is the bisector of \(\angle CAB\) and C - E - D. Prove that \(\angle DAE = \frac{1}{2} (\angle C - \angle B)\)
diagramNote: Fig. 3.63 — \(\triangle ABC\) with A at the lower-left, B at the lower-right and C at the top. D and E both lie on side CB, drawn in the order C - D - E - B. Seg AD is dashed with a right-angle mark at D showing \(AD \perp BC\); seg AE is solid and bisects \(\angle CAB\).
_note: DEFECT: the printed stem says "C - E - D" but Fig. 3.63 clearly draws the order C - D - E - B (the right-angle mark and the dashed AD are at D, which is nearer C than E). The figure is the correct configuration: since the result to be proved requires \(\angle C > \angle B\), the foot of the altitude D lies nearer C than the foot of the bisector E (checked numerically). So the collinearity string in the stem should read C - D - E. Transcribed faithfully as printed.
